rulebook: Illinois DCFS Rules 407, Licensing Standards for Day Care Centers (89 Ill. Adm. Code 407), July 7, 2025 - PT 2025.07 (through amendment at 49 Ill. Reg. 8719, eff. June 18, 2025)

findings.requirement: The center must have a written statement of purposes and policies as required by Section 407.250(c).
findings.quote: Statement of purposes and policies as required by Section 407.250(c);
findings.handbook_quote: This handbook is our written statement of purposes and policies.

findings.requirement: The center must file written delegation of administrative authority with the Department.
findings.quote: Written delegation of administrative authority as required by Section 407.70(b);
findings.handbook_quote: The board has filed with the Illinois Department of Children and Family Services (DCFS) a signed written statement that delegates day-to-day responsibility for licensing compliance to the director

findings.requirement: The governing body must file written policies outlining delegation of responsibility and lines of communication among governing body, staff, and parents.
findings.quote: The governing body shall file with the Department written policies outlining any delegation of responsibility for compliance with this Part and lines of communication among the governing body, facility staff and parents.
findings.handbook_quote: describes the lines of communication among the board, staff, and parents.

findings.requirement: The center must notify the Department immediately of major changes affecting regulated areas of operation.
findings.quote: The governing body, or others designated in writing to represent the center, shall notify the Department immediately of major changes affecting any area of operation regulated by 89 Ill. Adm. Code 407
findings.handbook_quote: We notify DCFS immediately of any major change affecting our operation

findings.requirement: The center must notify the Department in writing within 7 days after notice of legal action that may negatively affect operation.
findings.quote: The Department shall be notified in writing within 7 days after any notice of legal action against the center that may negatively affect its operation and/or ability to maintain the licensing standards.
findings.handbook_quote: We notify DCFS in writing within 7 days after receiving notice of any legal action against the center

findings.requirement: New staff orientation must include review of required documents, with review dates recorded in personnel files.
findings.quote: As a part of new staff orientation, the child care director and all staff shall review the following documents and the date of their review shall be recorded in the personnel files:
findings.handbook_quote: During orientation, the director and every new staff member review the Child Care Act of 1969, the Abused and Neglected Child Reporting Act, and the licensing standards

findings.requirement: A complete and current set of licensing standards must be available in an area accessible to all employees.
findings.quote: A complete and current set of licensing standards shall be available at all times in an area that is accessible to all employees.
findings.handbook_quote: A complete, current copy of the licensing standards is kept in the staff room

findings.requirement: The center must have written personnel policies available to staff at all times.
findings.quote: A day care center shall have written personnel policies available to the staff at all times.
findings.handbook_quote: our written personnel policies are available to staff at all times.

findings.requirement: Each child's record must contain a parent-signed statement that the parent received a summary of licensing standards and designated materials.
findings.quote: Each child's record shall contain a statement signed by the child's parent(s) or guardian indicating that he/she has received a summary of licensing standards and other materials designated by the Department for distribution.
findings.handbook_quote: At enrollment you receive this handbook, the DCFS summary of licensing standards, and other DCFS materials, and you sign a statement

findings.requirement: Suspected child abuse or neglect must be reported immediately to the Child Abuse/Neglect Hotline.
findings.quote: Suspected child abuse or neglect shall be reported immediately to the Child Abuse/Neglect Hotline as required by the Abused and Neglected Child Reporting Act, as amended.
findings.handbook_quote: Staff who suspect a child has been abused or neglected report it to the director, who looks into the concern and decides whether to call the DCFS Child Abuse/Neglect Hotline
findings.explanation: The handbook delays reporting by having the director investigate and decide whether to call the hotline instead of reporting suspected abuse or neglect immediately.
findings.fix: Every staff member who suspects child abuse or neglect reports it immediately to the DCFS Child Abuse/Neglect Hotline at 1-800-252-2873. Staff may tell the director, but reporting is not delayed while anyone looks into the concern.

findings.requirement: The child abuse reporting hotline number is 1-800-252-2873.
findings.quote: The telephone number for the reporting hotline is 1-800-252-2873.
findings.handbook_quote: DCFS Child Abuse/Neglect Hotline at 1-800-252-2873.

findings.requirement: The center must develop a written risk management plan addressing operational risks and emergency procedures.
findings.quote: The center shall develop a written risk management plan that identifies potential operational risks, specifies ways to reduce or eliminate the risks and establishes procedures to be followed in an emergency or crisis.
findings.handbook_quote: Our written risk management plan identifies risks in our operation, explains how we reduce them, and sets procedures for emergencies and crises.
findings.explanation: The handbook's risk management plan does not mention all required topics, such as selection and supervision of materials, toys, pets, and playground equipment, cleanliness of the building and grounds, maintenance and storage of chemicals and supplies, and an integrated pest management plan.
findings.fix: Our written risk management plan identifies potential operational risks, explains how we reduce or eliminate them, and sets procedures for emergencies and crises. It covers staff training, including universal precautions; building and vehicle upkeep; maintenance and storage of food service and maintenance equipment, chemicals, and supplies, including an integrated pest management plan; selection, maintenance, and supervision of education materials, toys, pets, and playground equipment; food service sanitation; cleanliness of the building and grounds; receiving severe weather and emergency alerts; and fire, tornado, and disaster preparedness plans.

findings.requirement: The center must carry public liability insurance with a single limit minimum of $300,000 per occurrence.
findings.quote: The day care center shall carry public liability insurance in the single limit minimum amount of $300,000 per occurrence
findings.handbook_quote: We carry public liability insurance of $500,000 per occurrence

findings.requirement: Accidents or injuries requiring professional medical care must be recorded and orally reported immediately to the parent and Department.
findings.quote: Any accident or injury requiring professional medical care, death or other emergency involving a child shall be entered into the child's record and orally reported immediately to the child's parent or guardian and to the appropriate local licensing office of the Department.
findings.handbook_quote: Any accident or injury that needs professional medical care, or any other emergency, is entered in your child's record and reported by phone immediately to you and to our DCFS licensing office.

findings.requirement: Required general and financial records must be maintained for 5 years.
findings.quote: Required general and financial records shall be maintained for 5 years.
findings.handbook_quote: general and financial records for 5 years

findings.requirement: Children's records must be maintained for 5 years after discharge from care or services.
findings.quote: Children's records shall be maintained for 5 years after the child has been discharged from care or services.
findings.handbook_quote: Children's records are kept for 5 years after a child leaves our program

findings.requirement: Accurate daily attendance records by group must be maintained for one year.
findings.quote: Accurate daily attendance records, by group, shall be maintained for one year.
findings.handbook_quote: daily attendance records by group for one year.

findings.requirement: Authorized Department representatives must be admitted during hours of operation to determine compliance.
findings.quote: Authorized representatives of the Department shall be admitted to the center during the hours of operation for the purpose of determining compliance with the Child Care Act of 1969 and standards set forth in this Part.
findings.handbook_quote: Authorized DCFS representatives are admitted at any time during our hours of operation.

findings.requirement: Information about a child's admission, progress, health, or discharge is confidential unless a parent grants written permission.
findings.quote: Information pertaining to the admission, progress, health, or discharge of an individual child shall be confidential and limited to facility staff designated by the child care director and Department representatives unless the parent(s) of the child has granted written permission for disclosure or dissemination.
findings.handbook_quote: Information about your child's admission, progress, health, or discharge is confidential and shared only with staff the director designates and DCFS representatives, unless you give written permission.

findings.requirement: The facility must have parent-signed confidentiality release forms specifying recipients and validity period.
findings.quote: The facility shall have confidentiality release forms signed by the parent(s) which specify to whom information may be released and the length of time the release form is valid.
findings.handbook_quote: Before we release information to anyone else, you sign a release form naming who may receive it and how long the release is valid.

findings.requirement: The center must have a written staffing plan that organizes staff for continuity of care and supervision.
findings.quote: A written staffing plan shall organize the staff and enable them to give the children continuity of care and supervision.
findings.handbook_quote: Our written staffing plan keeps the same primary teachers with each group every day, for continuity of care and supervision.

findings.requirement: Each staff person must be qualified for their position at the time of hire or promotion.
findings.quote: Each staff person shall be qualified for his or her position, as required by this Part, at the time he or she is hired or promoted.

findings.requirement: The director must ensure in-service training totaling at least 15 clock hours per year for each child care staff member.
findings.quote: The child care director shall be responsible for the planning and supervision of the program and activities of the children; orientation to newly employed staff; on-site supervision of all staff; and in-service training totaling a minimum of 15 clock hours per year for each member of the child care staff.

findings.requirement: The center must maintain the required staff-to-child ratios and maximum group sizes by age.
findings.quote: Whenever children of different ages are combined, as allowed by Section 407.190(d) below, the staff/child ratio and maximum group size shall be based on the age of the youngest child in the group.
findings.handbook_quote: When children of different ages are combined, such as during the first and last hour of the day, the ratio and group size follow the age of the majority of children in the group.
findings.explanation: The handbook uses the majority age for combined groups, but the rule requires the ratio and group size to be based on the youngest child in the group.
findings.fix: When children of different ages are combined, the staff-to-child ratio and maximum group size are based on the age of the youngest child in the group.

findings.requirement: When ages are combined, the staff-to-child ratio and maximum group size must be based on the youngest child in the group.
findings.quote: Whenever children of different ages are combined, as allowed by Section 407.190(d) below, the staff/child ratio and maximum group size shall be based on the age of the youngest child in the group.
findings.handbook_quote: When children of different ages are combined, such as during the first and last hour of the day, the ratio and group size follow the age of the majority of children in the group.
findings.explanation: The handbook's combined-age rule conflicts with the requirement to use the youngest child's age for ratio and group size.
findings.fix: When children of different ages are combined, the staff-to-child ratio and maximum group size are based on the age of the youngest child in the group.

findings.requirement: Children must not be left unattended at any time.
findings.quote: Children shall not be left unattended at any time.
findings.note: Beam marked this as covered, but the words it quoted don't appear in your handbook exactly as written (it may have joined two lines, such as two rows of a table).

findings.requirement: The center must have a written plan for encouraging parents to visit, observe, and participate, and parents may visit without appointment during normal hours.
findings.quote: The staff of the day care center shall have a written plan for encouraging parents to visit the center to observe and participate in their children's experience. Parents shall be allowed to visit the center without an appointment any time during normal hours of operation.
findings.handbook_quote: Our written plan for parent visits encourages you to observe and take part in your child's day.

findings.requirement: The daily program must be posted in the facility and provide required routines and activities.
findings.quote: The daily program shall be posted in the facility, and shall provide:
findings.handbook_quote: Each classroom's daily program is posted by its door.

findings.requirement: Written enrollment policies must not screen out children with disabilities and must allow reasonable modifications.
findings.quote: The day care center shall enroll only those children eligible under the center's written enrollment policies. The center shall not use eligibility criteria that screen out children with disabilities, and shall make reasonable modifications in policies, practices and procedures to accommodate children with disabilities.
findings.handbook_quote: We never use eligibility criteria that screen out children with disabilities, and we make reasonable changes to our practices so children with disabilities can take part.

findings.requirement: Before enrollment, parents must be provided program information and an opportunity to observe during hours of operation.
findings.quote: Prior to enrollment, the parents shall be provided information about the program and given an opportunity to observe during the hours of operation.
findings.handbook_quote: Before you enroll, we give you information about our program and invite you to observe a classroom at any time during our hours.

findings.requirement: The center must provide publicly available written statements covering required topics and give them to parents at enrollment.
findings.quote: The day care center shall provide publicly available written statements that include the following and that are given to parents at the time their child is enrolled in the facility:
findings.handbook_quote: At enrollment you receive this handbook, the DCFS summary of licensing standards, and other DCFS materials
findings.explanation: The handbook does not include every required written statement topic, such as procedures for personal belongings and, if applicable, water lead testing information.
findings.fix: Our written parent statements also include procedures for personal belongings brought to the center and, if our center is subject to water lead testing, where all water testing results are posted and any mitigation actions in place.

findings.requirement: The written parent statements must include hours of operation.
findings.quote: Admission, enrollment, and discharge policies and procedures: 8) A) Hours of operation;
findings.handbook_quote: We are open Monday through Friday, 6:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

findings.requirement: The written parent statements must include fees, payment plan, and policies regarding delinquent fees.
findings.quote: 4) Fees and plan for payment; 5) Policies regarding delinquent fees;
findings.handbook_quote: A non-refundable $100 registration fee is due at enrollment. Weekly tuition ranges from $160 for school-age children to $340 for infants

findings.requirement: The written parent statements must include arrangements for arrival and departure of children.
findings.quote: Arrangements for arrival and departure of children (time, location, transportation);
findings.handbook_quote: Families drop off and pick up children at the classroom

findings.requirement: The written parent statements must include a provision for emergency medical care, treatment of illness, and accidents.
findings.quote: Provision for emergency medical care, treatment of illness and accidents, which includes: A) A plan to obtain prompt services of physician and hospitalization, if needed
findings.handbook_quote: If a child needs a doctor or hospital, we call 911 or arrange care at Willow Ford Community Hospital, using the emergency treatment consent you sign at enrollment.

findings.requirement: The written parent statements must include visits, trips, or excursions off the premises and transportation used.
findings.quote: Visits, trips, or excursions off the premises and the transportation used for these visits, trips, or excursions;
findings.handbook_quote: Preschool and school-age classes take walking trips to Linden Park and the library and occasional museum trips in our center minibus.

findings.requirement: The written parent statements must include procedures concerning personal belongings brought to the center.
findings.quote: Procedures concerning personal belongings brought to the center;
findings.explanation: The handbook does not explain procedures for personal belongings brought to the center.
findings.fix: Please label all personal belongings with your child's name. We are not responsible for lost or damaged items, and we ask that children bring only items needed for the day.

findings.requirement: The written parent statements must include a policy regarding release of personal information on the child or family.
findings.quote: Policy regarding release of personal information on the child or family;
findings.handbook_quote: We never share personal information about your child or family without your written permission.

findings.requirement: The written parent statements must include planned means of communication between the center and parents.
findings.quote: Planned means of communication between the center and the parents;
findings.handbook_quote: We stay in touch through a daily report on our parent app, a monthly newsletter, the parent bulletin board, and conferences twice a year.

findings.requirement: Centers subject to lead water testing must inform parents where results are posted and any mitigation actions in place.
findings.quote: Day care centers subject to testing of water for the presence of lead shall inform parents where in the facility the results of all water testing (at, above or below 2.01 ppb) are prominently posted and any mitigation actions that are in place;
findings.explanation: The handbook does not tell parents where water lead testing results are posted or describe mitigation actions, if the center is subject to testing.
findings.fix: If our center is subject to water lead testing, we tell parents where all water testing results are prominently posted in the facility and describe any mitigation actions that are in place.

findings.requirement: The written parent statements must include behavior support and program transition policies.
findings.quote: 15) Planned means of communication between the center and the parents; 16) Day care centers subject to testing of water for the presence of lead shall inform parents where in the facility the results of all water testing (at, above or below 2.01 ppb) are prominently posted and any mitigation actions that are in place; and 17) Behavior Support and program transition policies.
findings.handbook_quote: If, after documented attempts to meet their needs, an infant, toddler, or preschooler cannot benefit from our program or their presence is harmful to the group, we will plan with you to find a better-suited program

findings.requirement: The facility must distribute a summary of licensing standards to parents when a child is accepted for care.
findings.quote: The facility shall distribute a summary of the licensing standards, provided by the Department, to the parents of each child at the time that the child is accepted for care in the facility.
findings.handbook_quote: At enrollment you receive this handbook, the DCFS summary of licensing standards, and other DCFS materials

findings.requirement: The center must give written notice that parents must provide a certified birth certificate or other proof of identity and age within 30 days of enrollment.
findings.quote: Provide a written notice to the parent of any child to be enrolled for the first time that within 30 days of enrollment the parent must provide a certified copy of the child's birth certificate or other reliable proof of identity and age of the child.
findings.handbook_quote: Within 30 days of enrollment, you must give us a certified copy of your child's birth certificate or other reliable proof of identity and age.

findings.requirement: All day care centers must have written transition policies outlining circumstances and process for transitioning children out of the program.
findings.quote: All day care centers shall have written transition policies that outline circumstances in which children may transition out of the program and what the transition process entails;
findings.handbook_quote: If, after documented attempts to meet their needs, an infant, toddler, or preschooler cannot benefit from our program or their presence is harmful to the group, we will plan with you to find a better-suited program and work with you and that program on a transition plan

findings.requirement: Providers must notify the Department of transition plans.
findings.quote: 1) All day care centers shall have written transition policies that outline circumstances in which children may transition out of the program and what the transition process entails; 2) Providers shall notify the Department of transition plans;
findings.handbook_quote: We notify DCFS of every transition plan.

findings.requirement: Parents have the right to withdraw a child, and the center must request a written statement of the reason for withdrawal.
findings.quote: Nothing shall preclude a parent's or legal guardian's right to withdraw his or her child from a day care center. A written statement from the parent or guardian shall be requested by the provider and kept on file, stating the reason for the decision to withdraw the child;
findings.handbook_quote: You may withdraw your child at any time.

findings.requirement: If a parent cannot provide a withdrawal letter, the licensee must maintain signed and dated documentation of the withdrawal request.
findings.quote: If parents/guardians are unable to provide a letter, the licensee shall maintain documentation that includes the requestor's name and relationship to the child, along with the withdrawal date. The licensee must also sign and date the documentation.
findings.handbook_quote: If you cannot provide a letter, the director records your name, your relationship to the child, and the withdrawal date, and signs and dates that record.

findings.requirement: Staff must conduct a daily pre-admission screening to determine if a child has obvious symptoms of illness.
findings.quote: Child care staff shall conduct a daily pre-admission screening to determine if the child has obvious symptoms of illness.
findings.handbook_quote: A teacher checks each child for obvious signs of illness before the child joins the group.

findings.requirement: Children must not remain on the premises more than 12 hours in any 24-hour period unless written parental confirmation is on file.
findings.quote: Children served in a day care center shall not remain on the premises for more than 12 hours in any 24-hour period, unless the parent's employment or training schedule requires more than 12 hours of day care and this has been confirmed in writing, by the parent.
findings.handbook_quote: A child may not stay more than 12 hours in any 24-hour period unless your work or training schedule requires it and you confirm this in writing.

findings.requirement: Persons not known to staff must provide photo identification before a child is released to them.
findings.quote: Persons not known to the staff shall be required to provide a driver's license (with photo), a photo identification card issued by the Illinois Secretary of State or other photo identification to establish their identity before the child is released to them.
findings.handbook_quote: Anyone not known to our staff must show a driver's license or other photo ID.

findings.requirement: When releasing a child to a contingency-list person, the center must record the person's name, date, and time.
findings.quote: When a child is released to a person authorized on the contingency list, the center shall maintain a record of the person's name and the date and time.
findings.handbook_quote: When a child goes home with someone on the contingency list, we record that person's name and the date and time.

findings.requirement: The time of each child's departure must be noted on a daily departure log and documented by the person receiving the child.
findings.quote: The time of each child's departure from the center shall be noted on a daily departure log and initialed, signed or otherwise documented by the person to whom the child is released.
findings.handbook_quote: The time of every departure is written on the daily departure log and initialed by the person picking up.

findings.requirement: A school-age child may leave unaccompanied only under a written policy or individual plan with written parental authorization.
findings.quote: When the center has a written policy or an individual plan for a specific school-age child, that child may be allowed to leave the center unaccompanied with written authorization from their parent or parents.
findings.handbook_quote: A school-age child may leave the center alone only under an individual plan with your written authorization stating the release time, how the child will travel and when they will return

findings.requirement: The center must have a written policy explaining actions if a parent does not pick up a child at the agreed time.
findings.quote: All day care centers shall have a written policy that explains to parents and staff the actions the center will take if a parent or guardian does not pick up, or arrange to have someone pick up, his or her child at the designated, agreed upon time.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not explain what the center will do if a parent does not pick up a child at the agreed time.
findings.fix: If a parent or guardian does not pick up a child at the agreed time, we follow our written late pickup policy. We contact parents and emergency contacts, keep the child safe and supervised, and, if needed, contact outside authorities after [number] minutes. Late fees, if any, begin after [time].

findings.requirement: The center must develop a guidance and discipline policy for staff use that is also provided to parents.
findings.quote: The day care center shall develop a guidance and discipline policy for staff use that is also provided to parents. Expulsion due to a child's pattern of challenging behavior is prohibited.
findings.handbook_quote: Staff sign this policy when hired, and parents sign it at enrollment.

findings.requirement: Written rules for all children must be established and available to children, parents, and staff.
findings.quote: Written rules for all children shall be established and available to children, parents and staff.
findings.handbook_quote: Our written rules for children are posted with pictures in every classroom

findings.requirement: Corporal punishment and other listed discipline practices are prohibited in all child care settings.
findings.quote: The following behaviors are prohibited in all child care settings: A) Corporal punishment, including hitting, spanking, swatting, beating, shaking, pinching and other measures intended to induce physical pain or fear;
findings.handbook_quote: We never use corporal punishment, including hitting, spanking, swatting, shaking, or pinching. We never threaten or withhold food, rest, or bathroom use, use abusive or profane language, or humiliate, shame, reject, terrorize, or isolate a child.

findings.requirement: Removal from the group must not exceed one minute per year of age and must not be used for children under 24 months.
findings.quote: Removal from the group to help a child gain control shall not exceed one minute per year of age. Removal from the group shall not be used for children less than 24 months of age.
findings.handbook_quote: A child who needs help calming down, including a toddler, may take a quiet break away from the group for up to ten minutes.
findings.explanation: The handbook allows a quiet break of up to ten minutes, but removal from the group may not exceed one minute per year of age and may not be used for children under 24 months.
findings.fix: A child who needs help calming down may take a brief quiet break away from the group for no more than one minute for each year of the child's age. Quiet breaks are not used for children under 24 months of age.

findings.requirement: Children must not be disciplined for toilet accidents.
findings.quote: Children shall not be disciplined for toilet accidents.
findings.handbook_quote: children are never disciplined for toilet accidents.

findings.requirement: Drivers transporting children must meet age, license, medical, and driving-history requirements.
findings.quote: The driver of a vehicle transporting children on behalf of a day care center, whether paid or unpaid, shall comply with the following requirements:
findings.handbook_quote: Our drivers meet Illinois requirements for age, license, medical exam, and driving record.

findings.requirement: Clinical behavior management plans may be developed with the parent and a professional clinician and documented in the child's file.
findings.quote: Clinical behavior management plans may be developed to meet the needs of a particular child if developed with the parent and a professional clinician. This must be documented in the child's file.
findings.handbook_quote: Any clinical behavior management plan is developed with you and a professional clinician and documented in your child's file.

findings.requirement: The required staff-to-child ratios must be maintained when transporting children.
findings.quote: The staff/child ratios as listed in this subsection shall be maintained.
findings.handbook_quote: Staff-to-child ratios are kept on every ride

findings.requirement: Federally approved age-appropriate safety restraints must be used when transporting children in vehicles under 10,000 pounds.
findings.quote: Age-appropriate safety restraints which are federally approved and labeled as such shall be used at all times when transporting children in vehicles having a gross weight of less than 10,000 pounds
findings.handbook_quote: each child rides in a federally approved car seat, booster, or seat belt suited to their age.

findings.requirement: The center must maintain a written emergency plan for transportation accidents, illness, severe weather, and other pertinent information.
findings.quote: A written emergency plan to be followed in case of accidents, serious illness, severe weather alerts, and other pertinent information shall be maintained.
findings.handbook_quote: The driver carries a written emergency plan for accidents, serious illness, and severe weather alerts.

findings.requirement: The center must maintain a written plan for scheduled transportation of children, including route schedule and safety precautions.
findings.quote: The facility shall maintain a written plan for scheduled transportation of children, which shall include:
findings.handbook_quote: Our written plan for scheduled school transportation lists the route schedule, the people authorized to receive each child, what we do if no authorized adult is present, and our safety precautions.

findings.requirement: A medical report on Department-prescribed forms must be on file for each child.
findings.quote: A medical report on forms prescribed by the Department shall be on file for each child.
findings.handbook_quote: Before your child starts, we need a medical report on the DCFS form showing the immunizations required by the Illinois Department of Public Health.

findings.requirement: The medical report must indicate the child received immunizations required by Illinois Department of Public Health rules.
findings.quote: The medical report shall indicate that the child has received the immunizations required by the Illinois Department of Public Health in its rules (77 Ill. Adm. Code 695, Immunization Code).
findings.handbook_quote: showing the immunizations required by the Illinois Department of Public Health.

findings.requirement: A child with a reportable communicable disease requiring isolation must be excluded from the center.
findings.quote: A child suspected of having or diagnosed as having a reportable infectious, contagious, or communicable disease for which isolation is required by the Illinois Department of Public Health's General Procedures for the Control of Communicable Diseases (77 Ill. Adm. Code 690) shall be excluded from the center.
findings.handbook_quote: or any reportable disease that requires isolation.

findings.requirement: A parent may request a written, signed waiver of immunizations, physical examinations, or medical treatment on religious grounds.
findings.quote: In accordance with the Child Care Act, a parent may request that immunizations, physical examinations and/or medical treatment be waived on religious grounds. A request for waiver shall be in writing, signed by the parent or parents, and kept in the child's record.
findings.handbook_quote: You may ask that immunizations, physical exams, or medical treatment be waived on religious grounds; the request must be in writing, signed by you, and is kept in your child's record.

findings.requirement: Children with diarrhea or rash with fever must not be admitted and must be removed if symptoms develop in care.
findings.quote: Children with diarrhea and those with a rash combined with fever (oral temperature of 101º F or higher or under the arm temperature of 100º F or higher) shall not be admitted to the day care center while those symptoms persist, and shall be removed as soon as possible should these symptoms develop while the child is in care.
findings.handbook_quote: Children with diarrhea, or with a rash together with a fever (101°F or higher by mouth, or 100°F or higher under the arm), may not attend while those symptoms last

findings.requirement: Children must be offered food at intervals of not less than 2 hours and not more than 3 hours apart, unless asleep.
findings.quote: Children shall be offered food at intervals of not less than 2 hours and not more than 3 hours apart, unless the child is asleep.
findings.handbook_quote: Children are offered a meal or snack about every four hours, unless they are asleep.
findings.explanation: The handbook offers food about every four hours, but food must be offered at intervals of no more than three hours apart.
findings.fix: Children are offered a meal or snack at intervals of not less than 2 hours and not more than 3 hours apart, unless the child is asleep.

findings.requirement: A child requiring a special diet must receive meals and snacks according to written instructions from parents, clergy, or medical provider.
findings.quote: A child requiring a special diet due to medical reasons, allergic reactions or religious beliefs shall be provided with meals and snacks according to the written instructions of the child's parents, clergy and/or the child's medical provider.
findings.handbook_quote: A child who needs a special diet for medical, allergy, or religious reasons receives meals and snacks that follow written instructions from you, your clergy, or your child's medical provider.

findings.requirement: Menus must be posted in an area accessible to parents and made available upon request.
findings.quote: Menus shall be posted in the kitchen, the classroom or other area accessible to parents, and made available to parents upon request.
findings.handbook_quote: Menus are posted outside the kitchen and each classroom, and copies are available on request.

findings.requirement: Children under 6 who are not in kindergarten or elementary school and remain 5 or more hours must have the opportunity to rest or nap.
findings.quote: Children under 6 years of age who are not enrolled in kindergarten or elementary school who remain 5 or more hours shall have the opportunity to rest or nap.
findings.handbook_quote: Children under 6 who are not yet in kindergarten and stay 5 hours or more have a rest time on their own labeled cot.

findings.requirement: Infants must be placed on their backs when put down to sleep, with limited exceptions.
findings.quote: To minimize the risk of sudden infant death syndrome, children shall be placed on their backs when put down to sleep according to the following guidelines:
findings.handbook_quote: Infants are placed to sleep on their backs or their tummies, whichever position helps them settle best.
findings.explanation: The handbook allows infants to be placed on their tummies to settle, but infants must be placed on their backs to sleep unless a physician gives written instructions for an alternative position.
findings.fix: Infants are placed on their backs when put down to sleep. A different sleep position is used only with written instructions signed by the child's physician.

findings.requirement: Soft bedding, bumpers, pillows, quilts, comforters, sheepskins, stuffed toys, and similar products must not be used or stored in cribs.
findings.quote: Soft bedding, bumpers, pillows, quilts, comforters, sheepskins, stuffed toys and other soft products shall not be used or stored in cribs.
findings.handbook_quote: Soft bedding, bumpers, pillows, quilts, comforters, sheepskins, and stuffed toys are never used or stored in cribs.

findings.requirement: The center must maintain a written policy regarding medications.
findings.quote: The day care center shall maintain a written policy regarding medications.
findings.handbook_quote: This is our written medication policy.

findings.requirement: Both prescription and non-prescription medication must be accepted only in the original container.
findings.quote: Both prescription and non-prescription medication shall be accepted only in its original container.
findings.handbook_quote: We accept prescription and over-the-counter medicine only in its original container.

findings.requirement: Prescription medication must be administered as required by a physician with appropriate parent releases on file and regularly updated.
findings.quote: Prescription medication shall be administered as required by a physician, subject to the receipt of appropriate releases from parents which shall be on file and regularly updated.
findings.handbook_quote: Prescription medicine must have the full pharmacy label and is given only as the physician directs, with your signed release on file and updated regularly.

findings.requirement: Over-the-counter medications may be dispensed per manufacturer instructions when provided by the parent with written permission.
findings.quote: Over-the-counter medications may be dispensed in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions when provided by the parent with written permission.
findings.handbook_quote: Over-the-counter medicine is given according to the manufacturer's instructions only when you provide it with written permission.

findings.requirement: The center must maintain a record of medication dates, times, dosages, prescription number, and administrator.
findings.quote: The day care center shall maintain a record of the dates, times administered, dosages, prescription number, if applicable, and the name of the person administering the medication.
findings.handbook_quote: A designated staff member records the date, time, dosage, prescription number, and their name for each dose.

findings.requirement: Topical products such as diaper ointment, sunscreen, or insect repellent must be approved by the parent in writing before use.
findings.quote: Any topical products, such as diaper ointment, sunscreen or insect repellant, whether supplied by the parent or by the child care center, shall be approved by the parent in writing prior to use on the child.
findings.handbook_quote: Diaper ointment, sunscreen, and insect repellent are used only after you approve them in writing.

findings.requirement: Staff in facilities caring for children ages 6 weeks through 6 years must show proof of Tdap and MMR or proof of immunity.
findings.quote: any staff person employed by a child care facility licensed to care for children ages 6 weeks through six years old is required to show proof/documentation of having received the following: One dose of the Tdap
findings.handbook_quote: staff show proof of Tdap and MMR vaccination or immunity.

findings.requirement: Staff who work with unpackaged food or food-contact surfaces must have IDPH-approved food handling training.
findings.quote: Staff who work with unpackaged food, food equipment or utensils, or food-contact surfaces must have food handling training that is approved by IDPH;

findings.requirement: The center's written risk management plan must include a staff vaccination policy consistent with CDC guidelines.
findings.quote: day care centers and homes include a staff vaccination policy, consistent with guidelines from the Centers for Disease Control, in the written risk management plan described in subsection 407.70(k)
findings.handbook_quote: It also includes our staff vaccination policy, which follows CDC guidelines: staff show proof of Tdap and MMR vaccination or immunity.
